name: vulcan_dreamchaser fairing
note: Launch vehicle render model (tools/make_rocket_models.py), vulcan_dreamchaser: fairing. Body frame: +Z toward the nose, origin at the aft end; engine bells below it. As vulcan with four solids and the long fairing; Dream Chaser nose down under it (the sim's spacecraft convention puts the berthing port on top), wings folded. One fairing half (the other is it turned 180 deg about +Z), in the stage's frame: separated, it falls away tumbling.

sources.subject: attitude
sources.value: +Z along the thrust axis (the sim passes it as 'velocity'), -Y (the ship's heat shield) down
sources.source: A rocket flies along its thrust axis; a gravity turn and an entry fly belly down.

sources.value: diameters and lengths rounded from the references; shapes (ogives, flaps, tapers) estimated from photographs
sources.source: ULA Vulcan Centaur page / User's Guide (2023): 5.4 m booster 33.3 m, Centaur V 11.7 m, GEM 63XL 1.6 m x 22 m, 5.4 m long fairing 21.3 m | Sierra Space: Dream Chaser launches on Vulcan Centaur VC4L (four solids, long fairing) | Sierra Space / Wikipedia 'Dream Chaser': cargo spaceplane 9 m long, 7 m wingspan (the wings fold to fit a 5 m fairing), lands on a runway (the KSC Shuttle Landing Facility); flies on Vulcan Centaur (VC4L) for CRS-2 | Sierra Space 'Shooting Star': the expendable cargo module on Dream Chaser's aft end, ~4.6 m long, solar arrays, jettisoned before the deorbit and destroyed on re-entry; berthed to the ISS by Canadarm2 (CRS-2 plan)

sources.value: white: white paint (operator liveries in launch photographs); grey: grey paint (Soyuz, Long March detail)
sources.source: Liveries from photographs; reflectance from the presets.
